correctness.rationale: The scalar certificate \(F(x)=\alpha x^2+\beta x+\pi(\cos x-1)\) has contacts at \(0\) and \(\pi/2\); its derivative changes sign exactly once in between, and remains positive thereafter. The analytic derivative proof covers all nonnegative real arguments. Integrating at an exact Fourier zero proves the sharp bound. Equality uses both sine and cosine cancellation; a symmetric three-atom family forces the limiting optimal ratio \(4/\pi-1\). The balancing estimate follows from \(\sin Y=S\cos(|Y|-b)\). Numerical checks supplement, but do not replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The sharp first-zero variance lower bound is a natural Fourier uncertainty invariant, but it cannot quantify how near-extremizers concentrate. The exact best quadratic remainder and balanced transport estimate provide a robust, dimensionless structural theorem for all finite-variance probability measures, with a sharp three-point obstruction; this is more than rediscovering the baseline threshold or a routine parameter substitution.
